answer: Memory-hard challenges deter Sybil attacks by issuing a periodic challenge pulse that forces agents to run a compute kernel across dedicated VRAM. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of dedicating physical memory bandwidth per identity, as cloned instances cannot share buses without failing latency thresholds. Each response acts as a cryptographic pearl confirming local capacity. However, this mechanism consumes significant electrical power and penalizes lightweight edge agents.
